Solution 3 gives $s_v = 3/2$ and $s_\rho = 1/2$, for a sum of 2. This matches my recollection of Lin and Xu's result on traveling waves for the 2D inhomogeneous Euler equations in a channel, which I believe states existence in $H^{3/2-}\times H^{1/2-}$ and nonexistence in $H^{3/2+}\times H^{1/2+}$ under the no-eigenvalue condition. I can't check the paper here, though. Solution 3's velocity argument is also shaky: it places the stream function in $H^{3/2-\tau}$, while the velocity is its derivative, so the sharp velocity exponent could differ. Solutions 1 and 2 have incorrect exponents, with sums 1 and 0 respectively.
